title: Martha Wright-Reed Just and Reasonable Communications Act of 2022
official_summary:
Martha Wright-Reed Just and Reasonable Communications Act of 2022

This act requires the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to ensure that rates and charges for payphone services or other calling devices, including advanced (e.g., audio or video) communications services in correctional institutions, are just and reasonable. When promulgating regulations or otherwise implementing this act, the FCC (1) may use industry-wide average costs related to providing telephone and advanced communications services, and (2) must consider costs for safety and security measures related to providing communications services in correctional facilities.

summary.headline: This law directs the FCC to make sure phone and video call rates in prisons and jails are just and reasonable.
summary.what_it_does: The act requires the Federal Communications Commission to ensure that rates and charges for payphones and other calling devices in correctional institutions are just and reasonable. This covers basic phone calls and advanced services such as audio or video calls. When writing rules or carrying out the law, the FCC may use industry-wide average costs. It must also consider the costs of safety and security measures in correctional facilities.

who_it_affects.group: People held in federal, state, and local correctional facilities
who_it_affects.how: The rates they or others pay for phone and video calls from facilities may be reviewed by the FCC under a just-and-reasonable standard.

who_it_affects.group: Families and friends who pay for calls to people in correctional facilities
who_it_affects.how: The cost of calls they make to incarcerated loved ones falls under the FCC's rate review.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that provide inmate calling and communications services
who_it_affects.how: Their rates and charges in correctional facilities must meet the FCC's just-and-reasonable standard, and the FCC will consider their industry-wide costs and security costs when setting rules.
The FCC must consider the cost of safety and security measures when setting the rules that affect calling services in their facilities.
